gender_gap.assumptions: The chapter's 85 cells reused unchanged (every cell has at least 30 women and 30 men); common age and work-from-home profile across cells; descriptive, not causal.
gender_gap.estimand: Descriptive averages of occupation-by-education cell contrasts in log hourly wage (women minus men, net of a common age and work-from-home profile): population-weighted (PATE-analogue), women-weighted (ATT-analogue), men-weighted (ATU-analogue), and the survey-weighted projection coefficient.
gender_gap.estimator: Weighted cell moments from PERWT; contrasts are within-cell differences in mean log wage minus the fitted age and work-from-home profile; the projection is WLS with cell fixed effects.
gender_gap.explicit_weights: PERWT for every weighted quantity; equal case weights for the OLS comparison.
gender_gap.implicit_weights: Projection: N_c p_c(1 − p_c) with p_c the female share. PATE-analogue: N_c. ATT-analogue: N_c p_c. ATU-analogue: N_c(1 − p_c).
gender_gap.randomness: The ACS sample and response process; sex is not assigned.
gender_gap.target_population: Wage and salary workers aged 25–64 in the 2024 ACS who usually worked 30+ hours a week for 40+ weeks in the past 12 months, had positive wage income, and were at work in the reference week.
gender_gap.title: The within-cell gender wage gap: the same averages, a second outcome
gender_gap.variance_estimator: SDR, 80 replicates; every contrast, cell weight, and average is recomputed per replicate; df = 79.

six_way.assumptions: 7 small cells merged within occupation (n ≥ 100, 30+ in each arm); common age–sex profile across cells; descriptive, not causal; TRANWORK construct caveat applies.
six_way.estimand: Descriptive averages of occupation-by-education cell contrasts in log hourly wage (WFH minus commuters, net of a common age–sex profile): population-weighted (PATE-analogue), WFH-weighted (ATT-analogue), commuter-weighted (ATU-analogue), and the survey-weighted projection coefficient.
six_way.estimator: Weighted cell moments from PERWT; contrasts are within-cell differences in mean log wage minus the fitted age–sex profile; the projection is WLS with cell fixed effects.
six_way.explicit_weights: PERWT for every weighted quantity; equal case weights for the OLS comparison.
six_way.implicit_weights: Projection: N_c p_c(1 − p_c). PATE-analogue: N_c. ATT-analogue: N_c p_c. ATU-analogue: N_c(1 − p_c).
six_way.randomness: The ACS sample and response process; no treatment assignment.
six_way.target_population: Wage and salary workers aged 25–64 in the 2024 ACS who usually worked 30+ hours a week for 40+ weeks in the past 12 months, had positive wage income, and were at work in the reference week.
six_way.title: Whose wage gap? Averaging the same cell contrasts in different ways
six_way.variance_estimator: SDR, 80 replicates; every contrast, cell weight, and average is recomputed per replicate; df = 79.

sloczynski.assumptions: The decomposition is an in-sample identity; reading its components as ATT and ATU requires unconfoundedness and linearity in p(X), which this descriptive analysis does not claim.
sloczynski.estimand: The cell-fixed-effect projection coefficient, re-expressed as ω₁·ATT + (1 − ω₁)·ATU, where ATT and ATU are average partial linear effects on WFH workers and commuters.
sloczynski.estimator: Linear propensity score p(X) from WLS of WFH on cells and age–sex terms; within-group projections of log wage on p(X); weights from group shares and within-group variances of p(X).
sloczynski.implicit_weights: ω₁ = (1 − ρ)V₀ / [ρV₁ + (1 − ρ)V₀] on the ATT; the smaller group gets the larger weight.
sloczynski.randomness: The ACS sample and response process.
sloczynski.target_population: Wage and salary workers aged 25–64 in the 2024 ACS who usually worked 30+ hours a week for 40+ weeks in the past 12 months, had positive wage income, and were at work in the reference week.
sloczynski.title: Smaller groups get larger weights (Słoczyński decomposition)
